enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

saml.description: SAML source can allow IdP-initiated logins, and the documentation explicitly warns that this request is not verified and may constitute a security risk.
saml.note: Do not treat acceptance of IdP-initiated login under this setting as an unexpected bug in SP-initiated request binding tests.

saml.description: The NameID value returned to the SP depends on the configured/default NameID policy and may be a hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, session ID, or email address.
saml.note: Different granted identifiers across tests may be by design if NameID policy differs.

saml.description: When a Source stage is used, the source flow is expected to resume the original flow via a dynamic in-memory stage; adding a User Login stage to the source flow changes behavior and directly authenticates instead of resuming.
saml.source: Source stage considerations / dynamic in-memory stage
saml.note: Misconfigured source flows can look like flow-coherence bugs but are documented behavior.

saml.description: Administrative changes to providers, applications, outposts, and related configuration are expected to propagate immediately; outposts also receive updates via websockets.
saml.note: A login succeeding or failing under newly changed admin configuration is by design. Only stale acceptance of old trust/config after change should be treated as suspicious.

saml.description: If a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
saml.note: Broad claims or permissions after an empty-scope request are by design and should not be flagged as over-authorization.

saml.constraint: For SAML I1 signature-validation tests, authentik as SAML SP only verifies signatures against a configured verification certificate on the SAML source. The fuzzer MUST create/configure the SAML source with an explicit trusted IdP certificate before running saml_cert_substitution or attacker-signed assertion tests; otherwise failures or successes cannot be attributed to signature verification behavior.

For SAML I1 issuer-validation tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure the SAML source's IdP issuer/entity ID and then send a mismatched assertion Issuer. If the source is created without an IdP entity ID, issuer comparison may be absent or ambiguous, so a successful login would not cleanly prove issuer-mismatch acceptance.

For SAML I1 default-config tests, authentik documentation states 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' may constitute a security risk because the request is not verified. The fuzzer MUST distinguish IdP-initiated acceptance from SP-initiated ACS validation tests; acceptance of IdP-initiated login when this option is enabled is by configuration and must not be reported as a generic proof-integrity bug.

For SAML I2 replay tests, use the SAME Assertion ID across two saml_login events when testing assertion replay or OneTimeUse replay. A second login with a fresh assertion ID is not a replay test and cannot detect missing replay protection.

For SAML I2 expired-assertion tests, the sequence MUST include a CONTROL saml_login with a valid assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Without a control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SAML source/provider setup.

For SAML I3 flow-coherence tests involving external source flows, authentik's Source stage suspends the current flow and later resumes it using a dynamic in-memory stage. The source's authentication/enrollment flow MUST NOT contain a User Login stage, or the original flow will not resume and results will reflect misconfiguration rather than coherence failure.
saml.source: Source stage considerations / dynamic in-memory stage

saml.constraint: For SAML I3 tests that depend on preserving request state across redirects, the executor MUST initiate the SAML flow first and preserve RelayState/InResponseTo linkage. Sending a fabricated ACS POST without first starting the SP flow will be rejected for request-state reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.
saml.source: SAML ACS semantics; flow context autosubmit/source docs

saml.constraint: For SAML I4 identity-binding tests, NameID format materially changes the identifier authentik receives: persistent may be a hashed ID, transient is session-based, emailAddress uses email, and other formats may use LDAP-derived attributes. The fuzzer MUST hold NameID policy constant across compared logins; changing NameID format changes the principal identifier by design and can create false collision or split-account results.

For SAML I4 account-linking/collision tests, avoid email-based NameID unless the test specifically targets email binding. authentik documentation warns email-based NameID is mutable because users may change email addresses, so merges/splits based on email can be by-design configuration outcomes rather than principal-binding flaws.

For SAML I4 tests involving IdP-initiated logins, do NOT compare them directly against SP-initiated flows for coherence or binding conclusions. authentik documents IdP-initiated login as a separate mode with weaker request verification properties; use a single initiation mode per test case.
saml.source: SAML Source example configuration / IdP-initiated SSO docs

saml.constraint: For SAML I5 audience/conditions tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly mutate or remove the SAML Conditions/AudienceRestriction in the assertion and compare against a valid control. Acceptance of a valid assertion without audience mutation is not evidence of missing audience enforcement.

For OAuth/OIDC verification after SAML login, session_token MUST be the access token, not any ID token. UserInfo is documented as returning claims for a valid access token, and using an ID token there will produce misleading failures unrelated to SAML security properties.

SAML login into authentik uses the SAML source ACS endpoint `/source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/`, not the SAML provider endpoints under `/application/saml/...`. The provider endpoints are for authentik acting as IdP to downstream SPs; SAML invariant tests for this profile must target the source ACS where authentik acts as SP.

For all SAML login tests, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve request state because authentik's SAML source is SP-initiated and the ACS consumes a response tied to the flow context. Use `initiate_saml_flow=true`; otherwise fabricated responses may be rejected for missing or mismatched request state/InResponseTo.

Allow IDP-Initiated Logins on a SAML source is documented as a security risk because the request is not verified and could be used to authenticate a user without interaction. For I3/I1/I2 tests, prefer SP-initiated flows; do not enable IdP-initiated login unless the test explicitly targets that insecure-by-design mode.

For I1 `saml_issuer_mismatch`, the SAML source's configured Issuer/Entity ID and upstream IdP metadata values must be explicitly set during setup. If issuer/entity-id trust is left implicit or imported loosely from metadata, a mismatch result may be ambiguous.

For I2 `saml_expired_assertion`, include a control SAML login without `expired_assertion=true` before the attack login. Otherwise a failed expired assertion test cannot be distinguished from a broken source/application/flow configuration.

For I2 replay tests (`saml_one_time_use_replay`, `saml_assertion_id_replay`), use the same SAML source slug and the same ACS endpoint across both submissions. Replays against different source configurations are not meaningful because authentik tracks sessions and trust per configured source.

For I3 `saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule`, MFA enforcement in authentik is flow-based. A valid bypass test must compare the same user under a password flow that includes Authenticator Validation or equivalent MFA enforcement versus a SAML source path for the same account. If the password flow itself lacks MFA, a successful SAML login without MFA is not evidence of bypass.

The Source stage documentation states that source authentication/enrollment flows must NOT contain a User Login stage when embedded via a Source stage, because that directly authenticates the pending user instead of resuming the original flow. For any I3 flow-coherence test involving Source stage composition, omit User Login from the source subflow or results are by-design flow behavior, not a vulnerability.

SAML NameID handling is configurable and may not equal the upstream identifier sent by the test. Default NameID policy can map to hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, transient session ID, or email address. For I4 principal-binding tests, do not assume NameID is the canonical downstream username unless the source/provider mapping explicitly binds on that attribute.

Email-based NameID is documented as unstable because users may change email addresses. For I4 collision or account-linking tests, avoid treating email NameID as a stable principal unless email mutability is intentionally part of the test.

When testing SAML account linking or collision behavior, remember that authentik sources can use property mappings and source flows to derive or transform identity attributes. The fuzzer MUST verify the actual granted identity via UserInfo/introspection rather than assuming raw NameID or email is stored unchanged.
UserInfo inspection uses the OAuth/OIDC access token returned by authentik after login. `session_token` for subsequent API calls must be the `access_token`, never an `id_token` or SAML assertion.

The OAuth token revocation and introspection endpoints require client authentication context for meaningful results. For cleanup and verification, use the same provider/client context that issued the token; introspecting or revoking under a different provider can fail by design.

authentik documents that when no scopes are requested, it treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. For I5 authorization-binding tests that rely on minimal claims, the fuzzer MUST explicitly request only the intended scopes; omitting `scope` broadens claims by design and can create false positives.

In authentik versions prior to 2025.10, the email scope always set `email_verified=true`; as of 2025.10 it defaults to `false`. For I4 `unverified_email_account_linking`, the fuzzer MUST account for version-dependent behavior and, on newer versions, explicitly configure any custom email scope mapping if it needs `email_verified=true` as a control.

SAML login testing against authentik as SP MUST target the SAML Source ACS endpoint `/source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/`, not the SAML Provider endpoints under `/application/saml/...`. The provider endpoints are for authentik acting as IdP to downstream SPs; the source ACS is where authentik consumes upstream SAML assertions.

For all `saml_login` tests, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve request state because authentik's SAML source is an SP and expects a matching request context. Use the ACS POST with `SAMLResponse` and `RelayState`, and keep `metadata.initiate_saml_flow=true`.

authentik documents that enabling `Allow IDP-Initiated Logins` on a SAML source may constitute a security risk because the request is not verified and could be used to authenticate a user without interaction. Therefore, for I3/I1 tests that rely on request-bound verification, the fuzzer MUST distinguish SP-initiated from IdP-initiated behavior and MUST NOT treat acceptance of IdP-initiated login as proof that SP-request correlation is broken unless that option was intentionally enabled.

For I1 `saml_cert_substitution` default-config testing, the fuzzer SHOULD create or use a SAML source/provider configuration with minimal trust settings and then submit the forged SAMLResponse. If signature validation material is explicitly configured, acceptance/rejection reflects that configuration; only default acceptance without configured trust should be treated as insecure default behavior.

For I1 `saml_issuer_mismatch`, authentik's SAML source configuration includes an explicit `Issuer/Entity ID` concept. The fuzzer MUST test both configured and unset issuer-trust scenarios separately: if issuer/entity ID trust is unset, acceptance may indicate skipped issuer binding by configuration rather than a bypass of an active check.

For I2 SAML freshness tests (`saml_expired_assertion`, replay, OneTimeUse), include a CONTROL login through the same SAML source without the mutation first. Without a successful control, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken source/flow configuration.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving authentik flows, remember that authentik flow planning can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid I3 test must show inconsistent handling of the SAME logical request/session, not merely that an admin changed stage/policy configuration and new logins followed the updated configuration.

For I3 source-stage resume tests, authentik's Source stage suspends the current flow and resumes it later, but only if the source's authentication/enrollment flows do NOT contain a User Login stage. If a User Login stage is bound in the source flow, the source flow authenticates directly instead of resuming the original flow. The fuzzer MUST avoid misclassifying this documented behavior as a flow-binding bug.

For I3 source-stage resume timing, the Source stage has a `Resume timeout`; if exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning on return. Tests that intentionally delay the upstream SAML round-trip MUST account for this timeout or they will produce false I3 failures.

For I4 principal-binding tests, authentik's SAML source `NameID Policy` materially changes which upstream identifier becomes the local username/identifier. Persistent may use a hashed ID, EmailAddress uses email, Windows may use UPN, and x509 Subject may use distinguishedName with fallback. The fuzzer MUST record which NameID policy is configured before interpreting identity merges or splits.

For I4 `saml_email_binding_collision` and account-linking tests, authentik documentation warns that email-based NameID is mutable by default because users may change email addresses. The fuzzer MUST distinguish NameID-based identity from email-based linking and MUST NOT assume email is a stable principal unless the configuration explicitly uses email as NameID or linking key.

For I4 display-name comparisons, authentik may derive the effective SAML identifier from hashed ID, UPN, distinguishedName, session ID, or email depending on NameID policy rather than echoing the raw attacker-supplied NameID string. The oracle MUST compare against the configured derivation mode, not only the literal submitted value.

For I5 `saml_no_conditions` and `saml_no_audience_restriction`, authentik as SP should validate Conditions/Audience on consumed assertions. However, if the test is run against authentik's SAML Provider endpoints instead of SAML Source ACS, results are meaningless because those endpoints issue assertions rather than consume them.

For OIDC-backed verification after SAML login, `session_token` MUST be the OAuth/OIDC `access_token`, not an ID token. authentik's UserInfo endpoint is documented as returning claims for a valid access token.

The OAuth revocation and introspection endpoints require client authentication context. The fuzzer MUST supply the appropriate `client_id` and `client_secret` (or equivalent provider credentials) when using `/application/o/revoke/` or `/application/o/introspect/`; otherwise failures are setup errors, not security findings.

authentik documents that the authorization code can only be used once and expires quickly. Any replay of an authorization code in mixed SAML→OIDC brokered flows is by-design rejected and should not be reported as anomalous flow behavior.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
